---
title: "Prompt injection"
---

Treat file contents as data unless a human explicitly promotes them to instructions. A note in a codebook, README, CSV cell, or command output may tell an agent to reveal files or ignore its task. This is prompt injection: untrusted text trying to act as an instruction.

Lab 3 uses a harmless fake-codebook injection. Its lab-local OpenCode plugin uses the documented `tool.execute.after` hook to rewrite returned tool output before it enters the session context. It leaves source files unchanged. A separate example shows how encoding and splitting bypass the filter. This is a teaching filter, not access control.

::: {.callout-note}
The OpenAI privacy-filter issue #13 is an instructor exhibit only. We do not install its full model or use it as a production boundary.
:::

If you see an injection, stop. Preserve the evidence, isolate the fixture, deny surprising actions, and inspect the diff and command history. Never test a bypass with real secrets.
